target.name: PreyVR jordi/robustness-body source and production-adapter fixtures

question: Does full-body state remain bound to the correct player and tracking coordinate context across discontinuities?
claim: The production adapters retain physical-crouch ownership and eye baseline across replacement players; a fixture emits an inherited stand request and retains 0.20 m eye lift at a changed standing baseline. Crouch can acquire before its compensation baseline is learned. The torso cache checks age without context identity, and estimator history retains the previous coordinate basis across a synthetic rebase (20 degrees vs 90 reset control). PlanBody retains planted world feet across a sub-metre owner/epoch discontinuity and reports valid despite a 0.388378 m shin-to-foot gap; Reset control reduces the gap to numerical noise. These are synthetic reproductions, not measured game occurrence.
method: MSVC 19.50.35729.0, VS 18 2026 x64 Release/static CRT. Fresh body DLL build and CTest 70/70. Probe CMake builds crouch.cpp including unchanged BodyFollow.cpp, torso.cpp including unchanged AnimIkTakeover.cpp and geometry.cpp linked to actual reviewed core. Native/XR boundary calls are stubbed, fixtures supply actor/pose/rig memory. Positive controls establish learned-eye crouch acquisition and compensation, initial valid PlanBody, reset torso and reset feet. Commands and control/variable definitions are in frozen REPRODUCE.md; exact outputs and numbered source are retained. No game process, injection or headset run. Initial missing link stubs/CRT setup errors were corrected before the recorded run and are not production findings.

identity.reason: Reviewed source commit is pinned; unchanged worktree and built DLL identity are recorded in identity.json.

instrument.reason: Probes execute the actual reviewed production adapters and pure solver with explicit synthetic boundaries. Frozen source/output establish tested paths.

control.reason: Normal acquired crouch compensation vs replaced actor/changed baseline/no baseline; retained torso history vs Reset under identical rebased input; retained feet vs Reset under the same valid body displacement.

scene.reason: Synthetic source fixtures only; no native game scene.

restore.reason: No production code, process or shared runtime state was mutated. Builds and probes use separate directories.

baseline.reason: Fresh Release build and existing 70/70 offline CTest pass (ctest.txt). This establishes only that baseline; additional probes reproduce missing invariants and do not approve the branch for integration.

limits: Synthetic LIVE harness evidence does not establish native ABI, transition frequency, performance, headset quality or that every ordinary recenter changes the raw OpenXR coordinate basis. Direct calls isolate adapter state; native inputs are not posted. Author FunkMockXR report is retained as provenance and is not independently rerun. Full-body source remains separate from integration, with four textual merge conflicts and previously fixed common robustness work to retain.

Production crouch-adapter probe with positive controls

Independent pure solver and planter fixture

next_action: Keep body separate; fix crouch ownership/baseline, coherent torso context publication and foot/pose state reset plus reachability. Add production-adapter regression assertions, resolve options conflicts preserving integration fixes, then perform bounded game and headset acceptance. Candidate for lifecycle-context playbook review, not bottleneck clearance.
